text.arabic_uthmani: ۞ قُلْ يَتَوَفَّىٰكُم مَّلَكُ ٱلْمَوْتِ ٱلَّذِى وُكِّلَ بِكُمْ ثُمَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمْ تُرْجَعُونَ

words.gloss_range: imperative report command that frames the following death-return statement as authorized speech
words.root_gloss_range: saying, utterance, statement, and doctrine; the local form selects a one-way command to speak

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the final passive return verb governed by the quoted speech frame

words.prose: {{ar:قُلْ}} ({{tr:qul}}) opens as a clipped report command: the singular messenger is ordered to voice a direct plural warning. The word turns everything through {{ar:تُرْجَعُونَ}} ({{tr:turjaʿūna}}) into one authorized utterance, answering the third-person denial in 32:10 with second-person address. Its short command shape gives an audible stop-start before the longer death-taking verb, while the supplied parallel to 67:24 keeps the death-return mechanism inside a decisive command-answer formula rather than private commentary.

topics.headline: commanded speech frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the death-return statement is relayed under command, not offered as the messenger's independent explanation.
topics.reason: The imperative is a 2ms command whose quoted complement runs through the ayah, so the following clauses are framed as authorized speech.

topics.headline: third-person denial becomes direct address
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the register shift from people spoken about to people confronted as you.
topics.reason: The command has an implicit singular addressee, while the quoted content turns to plural objects and subjects, matching the boundary from 32:10 into 32:11.

topics.headline: command answers surrounding speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the command as part of a larger speech-and-answer pattern around denial, death, and return.
topics.reason: The root recurs around the surah's speech challenges, and the supplied parallel to 67:24 supports a declarative challenge-answer frame without making that parallel govern the local syntax.

topics.headline: compressed command before expansion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the short command release into the longer taking verb that follows.
topics.reason: The compact imperative can support a cadence payoff: it is brief before the extended following verb, but it does not add a separate lexical sense.

words.gloss_range: complete taking or receiving in full in an imperfect active Form V frame with the addressees as object
words.root_gloss_range: fullness, completion, fulfillment, exact receipt, and death-taking; local form selects complete taking by the named agent, not simple killing or payment

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the delayed singular subject who performs the taking
the later sequential hinge separating taking from return

words.prose: {{ar:يَتَوَفَّىٰكُمْ}} ({{tr:yatawaffākum}}) makes death sound like complete taking, not bare destruction. The attached plural object puts the addressees inside the verb before the subject is named; only afterward does {{ar:مَلَكُ}} ({{tr:malaku}}) resolve the active singular agent. This is also the first -kum in the ayah, starting the you-chain that later reappears under custody, possession, and passive return. The imperfect form lets the act stand as an ongoing death-collection function, and the later {{ar:ثُمَّ}} ({{tr:thumma}}) keeps this full taking distinct from the subsequent return.

topics.headline: w-f-y completion in death-taking
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices death as a full collection or receipt before return, rather than as simple annihilation.
topics.reason: The root and Form V support complete taking, but claims about the soul persisting intact or obligation being fulfilled are limited to lexical pressure rather than asserted metaphysics.

topics.headline: taken addressees appear before the agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader first meets the addressees as the ones taken, then hears the agent who takes them.
topics.reason: The object suffix is attached to the verb, while the explicit subject follows as the singular agent.

topics.headline: imperfect form presents continuing function
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb presents the death-taking function as operative rather than as a single completed past event.
topics.reason: The imperfect active form licenses ongoing or future-facing force in the quoted warning.

topics.headline: first plural suffix starts the pronoun chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the first occurrence of the you-chain that later reappears under custody, possession, and passive return.
topics.reason: The 2mp object suffix shares the same addressee reference as later bound forms.

topics.headline: complete taking feeds the return sequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader follows a chain of custody: full collection by the death agent, interval, then return.
topics.reason: The local syntax joins the taking clause to the return clause through sequence; parallels to 6:61 and 7:37 are comparative evidence for death-taking agents, not replacement agents here.

words.gloss_range: singular construct head and nominative subject: the function-bearing angel who performs the taking
words.root_gloss_range: angel, messenger, authority, possession, dominion, and invested agency; local syntax selects the angelic agent under delegated authority

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the preceding complete-taking verb governed by the angel as subject
the construct title formed by angel and the death-domain complement
the genitive death-domain defining the construct title
the relative appointment clause specifying the agent
the later Lord phrase that names the final authority

words.prose: {{ar:مَلَكُ}} ({{tr:malaku}}) is not a generic angel mention. As the nominative subject of {{ar:يَتَوَفَّىٰكُمْ}} ({{tr:yatawaffākum}}) and the construct head of {{ar:مَلَكُ الْمَوْتِ}} ({{tr:malaku l-mawti}}), it names a singular office defined by death. The following relative clause, {{ar:الَّذِي وُكِّلَ بِكُمْ}} ({{tr:alladhī wukkila bikum}}), keeps that office delegated rather than autonomous, and the ayah later moves beyond the angel to {{ar:رَبِّكُمْ}} ({{tr:rabbikum}}) as the final authority, with 32:25 reserving final separation for the Lord. In recitation, the object-to-mīm transition also makes the addressed group flow tightly into the agent title.

topics.headline: singular construct agent of death
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a function-defined singular agent: the angel is subject of taking and construct head of the death title.
topics.reason: Case and iḍāfa evidence make the word the acting subject while binding it to the death-domain complement.

topics.headline: relative clause attaches appointment to the angel
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the appointment clause define the angel, not death in the abstract.
topics.reason: The masculine singular relative pronoun modifies the singular angel phrase.

topics.headline: authority and messenger derivations converge under delegation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that any authority carried by the angel is received and representative, not independent sovereignty.
topics.reason: The derivational debate and authority field are useful, but the following passive appointment clause narrows them to delegated agency in this context.

topics.headline: Quran-unique death-agent title
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this ayah concentrates the death-taking role in a singular titled office.
topics.reason: The supplied occurrence evidence treats the exact title as singular here, while plural angelic death passages such as 6:61, 7:37, and 47:27 remain comparative contrasts.

topics.headline: death agent is not final authority
topics.reader_payoff: The reader follows a hierarchy from angelic collection to Lordward return and later Lordly judgment.
topics.reason: The m-l-k/r-b-b field and 32:25 echo support the local hierarchy without shifting the grammatical subject of the taking clause.

topics.headline: sound binds object to agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the addressed object flow tightly into the named death agent.
topics.reason: The recitational transition supports a cadence payoff for the verb-object-to-subject movement.

words.gloss_range: definite genitive death-domain inside the angel title, not a finite killing verb
words.root_gloss_range: death, lifelessness, cessation, barren land, dead hearts, extinguished vitality, and causing death; local form selects the definite domain noun

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the later Lord phrase that receives the return after death

words.prose: {{ar:الْمَوْتِ}} ({{tr:al-mawti}}) makes death the definite domain that defines the angelic office. Because the word is a genitive gerund in the construct, it labels jurisdiction rather than making the angel the grammatical cause of death. The wider root field gives the domain the feel of stopped vitality, and the final stop in the word lets that cessation land audibly. The ayah immediately refuses to end there: death is followed by return to {{ar:رَبِّكُمْ}} ({{tr:rabbikum}}), while 32:14 extends the surah's permanence horizon after death.

topics.headline: definite genitive domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the angel is defined by the recognized domain of death, not by an indefinite death-like event.
topics.reason: The word is definite and genitive as the second term of the construct title.

topics.headline: death as stopped vitality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses death as a broad domain of ceased vitality, while the local title remains focused on human death-taking.
topics.reason: Barren-land, dead-heart, and extinguished-vitality senses widen the image, but the local construct with the death angel narrows the function to the death domain in this ayah.

topics.headline: noun domain rather than killing verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the grammar names the angel's domain rather than directly assigning killing causation through this word.
topics.reason: The local form is a gerund noun, not a causative death verb.

topics.headline: death is entry, not endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees death as the entry into a return sequence rather than the ayah's final horizon.
topics.reason: The local chain pairs death with return, and the supplied 32:14 echo supports death as entry into later permanence language rather than terminal closure.

topics.headline: final stop matches cessation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the death-domain noun close with a stopped cadence.
topics.reason: The sound observation supports cadence only and does not add a separate lexical branch.

words.gloss_range: masculine singular relative pronoun specifying the death angel through the appointment clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the masculine singular antecedent of the relative pronoun
the passive appointment clause governed by the relative pronoun

words.prose: {{ar:الَّذِي}} ({{tr:alladhī}}) locks the title back onto the appointment clause. Its masculine singular agreement points to {{ar:مَلَكُ}} ({{tr:malaku}}), so {{ar:وُكِّلَ بِكُمْ}} ({{tr:wukkila bikum}}) is not a floating comment about death in general; it is part of the death angel's definition. The relative form carries the noun phrase forward into passive delegation before the ayah turns to return.

topics.headline: relative pronoun specifies the angel
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the angel is defined by being appointed over the addressees.
topics.reason: The masculine singular relative pronoun modifies the singular angel phrase and introduces the defining relative clause.

topics.headline: form carries title into appointment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the title continue directly into the passive appointment clause without a new event boundary.
topics.reason: The relative has connective force rather than a root payload; it keeps the passive clause embedded inside the subject phrase.

words.gloss_range: an analyzer-split segment that belongs to the passive verb form, not an independent conjunction

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the repaired single passive appointment verb
the relative pronoun whose clause would be broken by a false conjunction reading

words.prose: {{ar:وُ}} ({{tr:wu-}}) has no independent conjunction payoff once the form is repaired. The segment belongs inside {{ar:وُكِّلَ}} ({{tr:wukkila}}), where it helps mark the passive pattern. Reading it as a connector would create a false break after {{ar:الَّذِي}} ({{tr:alladhī}}); reading it as verb morphology keeps the relative clause continuous and the appointment mechanism intact.

topics.headline: split segment belongs to passive verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader avoids inventing a new conjunction and keeps the appointment clause as one passive verb.
topics.reason: The bundle explicitly warns that MASAQ split the initial segment of the actual passive verb; the valid parse is the single Form II passive.

words.gloss_range: the second segment of the repaired passive Form II verb meaning was appointed or entrusted
words.root_gloss_range: entrusting, appointing, agency, representation, trusteehood, and reliance; local form selects passive delegated charge over the addressees

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the repaired passive Form II appointment verb
the prepositional complement marking the object under charge

words.prose: Read with the prior segment, {{ar:وُكِّلَ}} ({{tr:wukkila}}) says the death angel was appointed or entrusted, not self-authorized. Its passive Form II makes the authority derivative, and as a perfect passive appointment it stands grammatically settled before the ongoing death-taking function. {{ar:بِكُمْ}} ({{tr:bikum}}) gives that delegation a concrete object: the addressees are the ones placed under charge. The root's wider trust and agency field stays useful, but here it is narrowed to formal delegated jurisdiction within an authority chain that ends with the Lord; the supplied recording-angel parallel in 82:10-11 shows the broader delegated-angel pattern.

topics.headline: authority is delegated, not autonomous
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the angel's authority is received from an unnamed principal rather than intrinsic.
topics.reason: The verb is passive perfect Form II; attachment evidence leaves the assigning agent grammatically unstated while the ayah's hierarchy points beyond the angel.

topics.headline: appointed over the addressees
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the appointment has a governed object: the angel is charged over you.
topics.reason: The verb selects the bāʾ-governed pronoun as its complement, matching the custody frame.

topics.headline: settled appointment before ongoing taking
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the angel's appointment as already established before the death-taking function is performed.
topics.reason: The perfect passive appointment contrasts with the imperfect active taking verb.

topics.headline: trust field becomes representative agency here
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a root-field contrast: this is not the addressees trusting, but the angel being entrusted with charge.
topics.reason: Trust and tawakkul branches are real in the root family, but local passive appointment blocks reading the angel as the one placing trust.

topics.headline: delegated custody before return to Lord
topics.reader_payoff: The reader places angelic appointment inside a larger authority chain that ends with the Lord.
topics.reason: The supplied parallels to appointed recording angels in 82:10-11 support delegated angelic roles, while the local clause applies that structure to death collection.

words.gloss_range: preposition selected by the appointment verb to mark charge over the addressees

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the appointment verb that selects the bāʾ-governed complement
the governed plural addressee pronoun
the later directional preposition that opens the return clause

words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi-}}) narrows the appointment relation. After {{ar:وُكِّلَ}} ({{tr:wukkila}}), it is the bāʾ of charge or custody, not instrument, cause, or mere accompaniment. Because it remains attached to {{ar:كُمْ}} ({{tr:kum}}), the relative clause does not stop at 'was appointed'; it specifies appointed over the addressed group before the ayah moves from bāʾ-governed custody toward the Lordward {{ar:إِلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ilā}}) phrase.

topics.headline: bāʾ marks custodial charge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the preposition makes the addressees the object under delegated charge.
topics.reason: The local verb selects bāʾ for charge governance, narrowing away instrument, cause, or simple accompaniment readings.

topics.headline: preposition keeps appointment syntactically open
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the appointment completed only when the governed pronoun arrives.
topics.reason: The proclitic preposition fuses to the pronoun and prevents the passive verb from closing without its object of charge.

topics.headline: custody hands into return direction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader follows governed custody into the next governed direction toward the Lord.
topics.reason: The local sequence moves from bāʾ-governed charge to ilā-governed return destination.

words.gloss_range: 2mp suffix attached to the bāʾ, making the addressed group the object of appointed custody

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the earlier taking verb with the same plural addressee suffix
the custody phrase where the suffix is governed by bāʾ
the Lord phrase where the same suffix marks possession
the final passive verb encoding the same audience as subject

words.prose: {{ar:كُمْ}} ({{tr:kum}}) keeps the warning personal. The same plural audience already attached to {{ar:يَتَوَفَّىٰكُمْ}} ({{tr:yatawaffākum}}) now becomes the object of delegated charge in {{ar:بِكُمْ}} ({{tr:bikum}}); later it appears in {{ar:رَبِّكُمْ}} ({{tr:rabbikum}}) and inside {{ar:تُرْجَعُونَ}} ({{tr:turjaʿūna}}). The pronoun chain makes one group move through taking, custody, possession, and passive return, so the prior they of 32:10 is confronted as you.

topics.headline: the appointed charge is over you
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the angelic appointment is aimed at the addressed group, not at death in abstraction.
topics.reason: The suffix is governed by bāʾ as complement of the passive appointment verb and shares the quoted addressee reference.

topics.headline: one audience under changing roles
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the same you through direct object, custody object, possessed relation, and passive subject.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence links the second-person plural suffixes and final passive subject to the same addressee group.

topics.headline: third-person deniers become you
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the prior distant denial become direct confrontation.
topics.reason: The boundary row is coherent with the repeated 2mp morphology in the ayah.

words.gloss_range: sequential conjunction marking delay or rank progression between death-taking and return

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the death-agent title before the sequential hinge
the Lord phrase after the sequential hinge

words.prose: {{ar:ثُمَّ}} ({{tr:thumma}}) is the ayah's hinge. It blocks the taking by {{ar:مَلَكُ الْمَوْتِ}} ({{tr:malaku l-mawti}}) and the return to {{ar:رَبِّكُمْ}} ({{tr:rabbikum}}) from collapsing into one undifferentiated event. The particle allows interval and rank progression: first complete collection by a delegated agent, then return to the Lord. Its doubled mīm makes that pause audible as well as grammatical.

topics.headline: then separates collection from return
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a two-phase death-return sequence rather than immediate or unordered coordination.
topics.reason: The conjunction marks sequence with tarākhī, distinguishing it from immediate fa- or neutral wa-style coordination.

topics.headline: standalone heavy pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears and sees the transition as a held hinge in the middle of the ayah.
topics.reason: The standalone particle and geminated consonant support a cadence payoff that reinforces, but does not create, the sequential meaning.

words.gloss_range: fronted directional preposition governing the Lord phrase as endpoint before the passive return verb

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the fronted destination phrase governed by the preposition
the passive return verb whose endpoint is fixed in advance

words.prose: {{ar:إِلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ilā}}) fixes the endpoint before the passive verb arrives. The phrase {{ar:إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمْ}} ({{tr:ilā rabbikum}}) is fronted, so destination is heard before {{ar:تُرْجَعُونَ}} ({{tr:turjaʿūna}}); the return is directional and restricted, not merely a statement that an afterlife exists. The long final vowel gives the short preposition enough audible weight to open the final movement.

topics.headline: destination precedes return verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the destination is structurally foregrounded before the return itself is heard.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase precedes the passive verb while governing the Lord phrase as its complement.

topics.headline: direction to a specified endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees return as movement to a specified and exclusive endpoint.
topics.reason: The directional preposition marks endpoint; fronting supports destination restriction without adding an unstated alternative destination.

topics.headline: long vowel carries final movement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the directional particle carry the clause toward the Lord phrase.
topics.reason: The dagger-alif observation supports a small recitational payoff within the directional role.

words.gloss_range: singular construct Lord phrase with plural possessive suffix, governed by the fronted endpoint preposition
words.root_gloss_range: lordship, ownership, sustaining care, upbringing, cultivation, mastery, and governance; local phrase names the addressees' own Lord as return endpoint

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the earlier custody phrase with the same plural suffix

words.prose: {{ar:رَبِّكُمْ}} ({{tr:rabbikum}}) makes the endpoint personal and sovereignly relational: not a neutral destination, but your Lord. The singular construct gathers the plural addressees under one authority, and the root field brings ownership and nurturing development into the title. After the angelic charge in {{ar:بِكُمْ}} ({{tr:bikum}}), the same plural suffix returns as possession, so custody gives way to belonging and final destination. The movement from the open directional vowel into the repeated r-b-b pressure makes the destination phrase cohere audibly. The phrase also joins the broader return-to-Lord formula (2:28; 6:60; 23:79; 36:83) while answering 32:10 and anticipating 32:12.

topics.headline: your Lord as governed endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the return endpoint is relationally specified as your Lord.
topics.reason: The phrase is genitive under the directional preposition and definite through the possessive construct.

topics.headline: owner and cultivator, not merely ruler
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears Lordship as ownership and sustaining cultivation, while the local phrase remains a return destination.
topics.reason: The r-b-b family supports ownership and nurturing development; local grammar narrows that field to the named endpoint of return.

topics.headline: one Lord over the plural you
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the plural audience gathered under a singular Lord relation.
topics.reason: The singular noun carries a plural suffix, preserving collective address without pluralizing the authority.

topics.headline: from charge over you to your Lord
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the same you shifting from object of angelic custody to possessed relation with the Lord.
topics.reason: The repeated suffix has the same addressee reference but a new syntactic role inside the Lord phrase.

topics.headline: local phrase enters return formula and surah thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the final destination phrase as both a surah-local answer and part of a wider return-to-Lord formula.
topics.reason: The supplied evidence links this phrase to 32:10, 32:12, and formulaic parallels at 2:28, 6:60, 23:79, and 36:83 without overriding the local syntax.

topics.headline: sound binds direction to Lord phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the directional phrase cohere as it moves into the Lord title.
topics.reason: The sound observation supports cohesion between the preposition and the governed Lord phrase.

words.gloss_range: imperfect Form IV passive: the addressees are made to return to the already fronted endpoint
words.root_gloss_range: return, being sent back, restoration, reference point, taking back, rebound, and recurrence; local form selects externally caused passive return

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the fronted destination phrase that fixes the endpoint before the verb
the active variant used as agency contrast for the standard passive
the earlier passive appointment verb paired with the final passive return

words.prose: {{ar:تُرْجَعُونَ}} ({{tr:turjaʿūna}}) closes the ayah with imposed return. The destination has already been fixed by {{ar:إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمْ}} ({{tr:ilā rabbikum}}), so the final verb foregrounds the addressees as passive patients of a return they do not control. The active variant {{ar:تَرْجِعُونَ}} ({{tr:tarjiʿūna}}) exposes the agency contrast, but the local standard reading selects being returned. As an imperfect, it presents that return as a certain coming event rather than a completed past. Root pressure makes the movement a return toward source and authority, and its final position lets the death-taking chain land on being brought back. Together with {{ar:وُكِّلَ}} ({{tr:wukkila}}), it pairs the appointed angel and returned humans as recipients of action under higher agency, and the announced passive return is revoiced as a plea in 32:12.

topics.headline: you are returned, not self-returning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the addressees are acted upon in the final return.
topics.reason: The local form is passive Form IV with the addressees as 2mp subject and an unstated returning agent.

topics.headline: variant shows agency pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees what changes if the verb is active: agency shifts toward the addressees, while the standard local reading removes it.
topics.reason: The accepted active variant is valid contrast evidence, but it does not govern the standard local passive parse.

topics.headline: return implies source and reference point
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the return as movement back toward an origin or authority, not random motion.
topics.reason: The root family supports return-point, reclaiming, and rebound imagery; local grammar narrows this to passive return to the named Lord.

topics.headline: imperfect passive keeps return pending and certain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the return is presented from the command as a certain coming event rather than a completed past.
topics.reason: The imperfect passive differs from a completed perfect return form.

topics.headline: final passive return formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah end inside a familiar passive return-to-Lord pattern, sharpened by the local death-agent mechanism.
topics.reason: The r-j-ʿ/r-b-b pairing matches the fronted destination phrase; supplied parallels such as 2:28 and 36:83 support formulaic recognition.

topics.headline: angel and humans both under higher agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that both the appointed angel and returned humans are grammatically acted upon.
topics.reason: The ayah pairs passive appointment of the angel with passive return of the addressees, placing both under a higher unnamed agency.

topics.headline: announcement becomes plea in 32:12
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the announced return become a plea for return in the next ayah (32:12).
topics.reason: The same root recurs in 32:12 as a request from another discourse position, which preserves a concrete surah-local echo.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: يَتَوَفَّىٰكُم مَّلَكُ ٱلْمَوْتِ ٱلَّذِى وُكِّلَ بِكُمْ ... تُرْجَعُونَ
baseline_models.mechanism: Complete taking, a named angelic agent, passive commissioning, death, and a later passive return form a two-stage custody chain rather than an accidental cessation.

activation_trace.role: Completion without deficit makes the taking exhaustive rather than partial.
Taking the self supplies the death operation while retaining the concrete sense of reception into custody.
The angel branch identifies a messenger-agent rather than an impersonal event.
Departure of life supplies the biological threshold at which custody changes.
A commissioned keeper competent to preserve makes the transfer an assigned operation.
Being sent back supplies the second movement after the completed taking.

changed_reading.before: Death occurs and people later go back to God.
changed_reading.after: Each person is fully taken by a commissioned custodian at death and only afterward returned to the Lord.

baseline_models.mechanism: The passive return terminates at the possessor and sustainer; the split mapped growth branch keeps alive a second image of return to the source that raised the person, not movement to an arbitrary destination.

activation_trace.role: Lordship, ownership, and command identify the terminal authority of the return.
Progressive tending and completion make the destination also the source of formation.
The non-dominant growth target activates nurture and emergence as a latent origin-image.
Return to a prior direction or state turns the endpoint into reversion to origin.
Arrival at an appointment lets the initial taking anticipate the terminal meeting.

changed_reading.before: The Lord is simply the destination after death.
changed_reading.after: Return closes a developmental arc by restoring the fully taken person to the authority that owned, tended, and raised that life.

baseline_models.mechanism: The commanded utterance and the final return can be heard as a compact answer circuit: speech is issued now, while the return branch also carries reply and speech coming back to its speaker.

activation_trace.role: Audible utterance launches the verse as an answer rather than silent description.
A thing's saying as its indication lets the death mechanism itself function as proof-bearing speech.
Reply and speech returning to its source links bodily return with an answer coming back.

changed_reading.before: The imperative merely introduces information about death.
changed_reading.after: The utterance stages an answer whose content and addressees will both be returned, making death itself the reply to denial.

context_deltas.mechanism: Descent from the Lord, management of the affair across heaven and earth, and ascent to Him supply a directional governance circuit; the delegated taking and return of persons becomes one human passage through that circuit.

activation_trace.role: Delivery downward from the Lord establishes the circuit's outbound vector.
Managing an affair by regard to its outcome supplies coordinated direction rather than random motion.
The affair as a governed state provides the domain through which the traffic moves.
Ascent upward supplies the inbound vector toward Him.
The keeper carrying out an assigned matter localizes the circuit in an accountable agent.
Return completes the personal inbound movement.

structural_cues: 32:2 locates descent from the Lord; 32:5 moves from heaven to earth and then to Him; 32:11 repeats then and to your Lord.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies descent, managed affair, ascent, delegation, and return; I infer one coordinated traffic pattern linking them. A live alternative is that the vectors are rhetorical parallels rather than phases of one process.

changed_reading.before: Death is an isolated event followed by a separate return.
changed_reading.after: Death-taking is the personal inbound leg of an already active down-and-up order of divine governance.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding fear of becoming lost in earth is answered by exhaustive taking: apparent dispersal cannot create a custody deficit, and return brings the recovered person to the denied meeting and renewed creation.

activation_trace.role: Loss of the thing supplies the deniers' feared failure mode.
Loss of preservation sharpens the objection as a custody problem.
Creative bringing-into-being states the reconstruction they doubt.
New occurrence after severance supplies the discontinuity their question cannot bridge.
Two sides coming face to face identifies the denied endpoint as encounter, not mere relocation.
Taking in full with no deficit directly blocks the loss scenario.
Return carries the fully recovered person across the alleged discontinuity.

structural_cues: 32:10's objection is immediately followed by the command to answer in 32:11, and the second-person plural keeps the same addressees in view.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies loss in earth, new creation, denied meeting, and complete taking; I infer that the completeness verb answers the loss objection as a recovery guarantee. Alternatively, it may be a conventional death verb without deliberate polemic against dispersal.

changed_reading.before: The angel takes people when they die.
changed_reading.after: The assigned taker loses none of the person to earthly dispersal; exhaustive recovery is what makes renewed creation and meeting possible.

context_deltas.mechanism: The staged formation from clay, extracted lineage, fashioning, and life-bearing spirit makes death-taking a reverse handoff of an assembled and enlivened person; return closes the same formation arc at its nurturing source.

activation_trace.role: Creative production supplies the first assembly stage that death later reverses.
Beginning paired with return or repetition explicitly opens a start-and-restoration arc.
An extracted essence supplies a materially selected input to human formation.
Sending breath into something supplies the transition from formed matter to living recipient.
The spirit by which the body lives identifies what makes the formed body animate.
Taking the self reverses reception of life without reducing the person to discarded matter.
The growth target makes the Lordward endpoint resonate with the source of nurture and emergence.

structural_cues: Repeated then markers stage lineage, fashioning, animation, death-taking, and return as ordered transitions rather than one undifferentiated event.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies sequential formation, animation, taking, and return; I infer a reverse handoff from the created order back to its source. A live alternative is that creation only proves power over resurrection and does not specify a reversed process.

changed_reading.before: Death removes life from an already existing person.
changed_reading.after: Death is the reverse custody handoff of a deliberately formed and enlivened person, whose return completes the originating act.

context_deltas.mechanism: The denial of any independent patron or intercessor beside God prevents the angel's role from becoming rival sovereignty: the angel stands over death only because the task has been assigned, and the chain terminates at the Lord.

activation_trace.role: Standing over and administering an affair is denied as an independent role apart from God.
An intercessor joining another is likewise denied as an autonomous mediating power.
The angel remains a real personal agent within the bounded role.
Entrusting an affair to another marks the angel's authority as derived.
Competent preservation defines the content, not the source, of the agent's authority.
Lordship and ownership reserve ultimate authority for the endpoint of return.

structural_cues: The passive commissioning suppresses the assigner's name locally, while the final phrase names the Lord as the destination and controlling authority.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies denied independent mediation, an angel, passive assignment, and return to the Lord; I infer a contrast between bounded agency and autonomous power. Alternatively, 32:4 may deny only salvific patrons, without commenting on operational agents.

changed_reading.before: The angel of death controls the moment of death.
changed_reading.after: The angel performs a bounded custodial commission whose real agency displays, rather than competes with, the Lord's exclusive authority.

context_deltas.mechanism: The promised passive return is followed by bowed criminals requesting a different return so they can act again; the first is compelled encounter, while the requested replay of earthly agency is unavailable because the meeting was neglected.

activation_trace.role: The lowered head and gaze embody recognition after the promised return has occurred.
A return away from wrongdoing supplies the criminals' requested second chance.
Face-to-face encounter defines what the promised Lordward return actually reaches.
Neglecting and then being left supplies the asymmetry that closes the requested replay.
The imposed return delivers the addressees to encounter, not back to their prior opportunity.
Arrival at the appointed meeting makes the transfer terminal rather than provisional.

structural_cues: The sequence distinguishes you will be returned in 32:11 from return us in 32:12, changing the same root from passive destination to an unanswered request for renewed agency.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two adjacent returns, bowed recognition, meeting, and neglect; I infer that the second request exposes the irreversibility of the first. Alternatively, the request may simply dramatize regret without defining the mechanics of 32:11.

changed_reading.before: Return means coming back after death.
changed_reading.after: The promised return is compelled arrival for encounter, not a replay of earthly life; only then do the addressees ask for the unavailable reverse journey.

context_deltas.mechanism: A binding word, recompense that answers deeds and can resemble full debt collection, and the Lord's separating judgment turn exhaustive death-taking into a case transfer for complete settlement.

activation_trace.role: A fixed obligation that has become due supplies the enforceable basis for the transfer.

Judgment separating right from wrong identifies the Lordward endpoint as adjudication.
Full taking with no deficit ensures that the whole case reaches settlement.
The owner and sovereign is also the authority before whom settlement occurs.

structural_cues: The focus transfers every second-person addressee, while later contrasts sort outcomes by what they did and culminate in the Lord's judgment.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a due word, deed-matched recompense, separating judgment, and exhaustive taking; I infer a legal-accounting handoff from custody to settlement. Alternatively, these may be adjacent eschatological themes without an administrative case-transfer relation.

changed_reading.before: The angel transports the dead to their Lord.
changed_reading.after: The angel transfers the complete person and record into a Lordward process where a due claim is separated and settled without deficit.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus's imposed return opens into two later return patterns: repeated forcible replacement into fire when exit is attempted, and a nearer correction intended to produce voluntary turning back.

activation_trace.role: Return after attempted departure supplies an iterative forced recurrence.
Turning back from wrongdoing supplies the still-open corrective alternative before final return.
The passive return establishes the unavoidable outer movement within which later recurrences differ.
A death-state as a condition, not only an instant, permits the return to open into an enduring outcome.

structural_cues: The focus passive and 32:20's passive re-insertion both remove the subject's control, while every time in 32:20 marks recurrence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies passive return, repeated forced re-entry, and a hoped-for moral return; I infer that 32:11 initiates a field of involuntary and voluntary return-patterns. Alternatively, 32:20's repetition may describe only punishment after the single Lordward return.

changed_reading.before: Return to the Lord is one neutral journey.
changed_reading.after: The unavoidable return ends neutrality: prior voluntary turning remains possible, but afterward some are subjected to a repeated forced return whenever they seek exit.

context_deltas.mechanism: Repeated public allegations, speculative questions about re-creation and judgment, and commanded answers turn the focus command into a counter-utterance that closes debate by naming the mechanism and deadline of return.

activation_trace.role: False attribution makes the first public saying an allegation that demands an answer.
Speech operating as supposition frames earthly loss and new creation as a skeptical hypothesis.
A saying circulating among people extends the challenge to the timing of judgment.
The commanded audible reply answers the circulating challenge in the same speech mode as the focus.
Opening as decisive judgment supplies the deadline that argumentative speech cannot postpone.
Waiting or granting respite, here denied, closes the temporal escape from the answer.
The focus command voices the central counter-answer: assigned taking followed by return.

structural_cues: The ordered chain says in 32:3, says in 32:10, say in 32:11, they say in 32:28, and say in 32:29 alternates challenge and response.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies recurring speech verbs, skeptical content, commanded replies, judgment, and denied respite; I infer a designed challenge-answer chain in which 32:11 is a decisive counter-utterance. Alternatively, the repeated speech formulas may organize discourse without making death itself argumentative.

changed_reading.before: Say merely introduces a doctrinal proposition.
changed_reading.after: Say inserts a performative counter-answer into repeated skeptical speech: the appointed taking guarantees the return that their questions try to defer.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it maps water, barren land, and germination onto personal death and return. It remains anchored in the focus's own dead-land and returning-water branches plus its delegated transport, but downstream prose should present it only as a governed reconstitution analogy, not as a lexical equation or cyclical reincarnation claim.

activation_trace.role: Driving and conducting water supplies a governed conveyance parallel to assigned taking.
Land stripped of vegetation supplies the materially death-like receiving state.
Germination and growth supply visible reconstitution after governed conveyance.
Dead land already latent in the focus root provides the cross-domain hinge.
Returning rain or water gives the focus return an ecological circulation image.
A preserving agent keeps the analogy about governed conveyance rather than spontaneous cycling.

changed_reading.before: Death-taking removes a person from life and return follows later.
changed_reading.after: As an exploratory material analogy, assigned death-taking resembles water conducted into barren ground: a governed transfer whose hidden horizon is reconstitution.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising and form-distant because it activates the packet's non-dominant ق ل ل mapping beneath the imperative of speech. It is still formally anchored in the supplied split inventory and reinforced by the later repeated command, but prose should label it a sound-form latent activation, never a translation of the imperative.

activation_trace.role: Bearing, rising, and setting out makes the short command feel like lifting the burden of the answer into public speech.
Agitation and unstable movement give the utterance a disruptive effect on settled denial.
The repeated command later bears a second terminal answer, sustaining the form-level pattern.

changed_reading.before: The command simply asks the messenger to speak.
changed_reading.after: At the level of latent form, the compact command bears and raises a destabilizing answer that the addressees must eventually undergo.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it hears death as compelled yielding to truth rather than only loss of life. The focus root explicitly supplies that branch and the next scene supplies bowed recognition before a truth that has become due; prose should retain biological death as primary and mark yielding as an affective-legal overlay.

activation_trace.role: Submission to truth turns death into the point where resistance finally yields.
Lowered heads and sight embody the posture of compelled acknowledgment after return.
Truth fixed against falsehood supplies what the returning denier can no longer evade.
Return delivers that yielded person to the authority of the truth acknowledged.

changed_reading.before: Death ends bodily life before return.
changed_reading.after: Death also marks the compelled collapse of resistance: the person yields to the truth and is returned in a posture of recognition.

strongest_changes: Complete taking answers the immediately preceding fear that persons become lost in earth.
Delegated death-taking becomes the human inbound leg of a larger descent, governance, and ascent circuit.
The first compelled return is distinguished from the criminals' later, unavailable request for a replay of earthly agency.
Custody becomes bounded agency and full settlement rather than independent angelic sovereignty or neutral transport.
summary.what_was_special: The compact verse behaved like a transfer protocol: complete recovery, assigned custody, return to originating authority, and an answer to skeptical speech. Split-root growth and bearing images, plus dead-land circulation, preserved additional exploratory readings without displacing the primary mechanism.
remaining_uncertainties: The down-and-up context may be a rhetorical spatial parallel rather than one literal administrative circuit.
The creation sequence clearly supports restoration, but a strict reverse-handoff mechanism remains reader-supplied.
The ق ل ل, ecological, and yielding activations are branch-backed but should remain explicitly exploratory or secondary.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Death is complete receipt, the opposite of being lost.** `و ف ي:B002` gives receiving the soul in full as death, grounded in `و ف ي:B001`, complete fullness without shortfall. The answer directly follows 32:10’s *ḍalalnā fī al-arḍ*, whose activated image was disappearance and failed location. **Inferred arrow:** complete taking with no shortfall -> preservation through the transition called death. *Yatawaffākum* corrects the prior speakers’ verb: from their side they disappear; from the agent’s side they are fully received.

2. **Delegated agency preserves, rather than divides, the chain of authority.** `و ك ل:B001` supplies handing an affair to an authorized agent, and `و ك ل:B006` supplies the one who undertakes and guards what is entrusted. The relative clause limits the death-angel to an assigned role; *thumma ilā rabbikum* names the ultimate destination. **Inferred arrow:** delegation of the taking-stage -> reliable execution of that stage, not transfer of final sovereignty. The angel reads as an accountable function inside the governance described in 32:4–5.

3. **Return restores the origin as destination.** `ر ج ع:B001` covers return, or being sent back, to a prior place, owner, or state. Its passive grammar follows complete taking and points specifically “to your Lord,” while the beginning in 32:7 and renewal question in 32:10 supply the arc’s other end. **Inferred arrow:** preservation through death -> restoration to the originating authority. *Turjaʿūn* reads as completion of an origin–transfer–return circuit, not undirected revival.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 32:12 made two returns diverge: compulsory return to the Lord in 32:11 is certain, but the offenders' requested return to productive action is refused by the closed time of judgment. 32:16 then supplied the missing timely alternative, showing voluntary response before that compulsory return.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bu dalı sesle ortaya çıkarılan söz ve harflerden kurulu sözlü ifade olarak verir. Geçici çerçeve aynı çekirdeği taşıyor; dil organı, hükümdar unvanı ve mecazi yan kullanımlar bu dalın dışında kalır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal çıplak söz söyleme ve söylenmiş söz çekirdeğidir; organ, unvan, söylenti ve mecazlar ayrı dallardır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam bare olduğu için tanım çıplak söyleme ve sözlü ifade anlamıyla sınırlıdır.

concept_map.definition: Bir düşünceyi veya sözü sesli biçimde dışa vurma ve böyle dışa vurulmuş harfli sözlü ifade anlamıdır.

facets.statement: Çekirdek işlem, sözü sesli olarak dışa çıkarmaktır.
Söylenen şey tek söz, cümle, şiir veya konuşma ölçeğinde olabilir.
Ad biçimleri aynı söylenmiş söz alanında toplanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, sözü sesle dışa çıkarılan ve harflerden oluşan sözlü ifade çekirdeğinde toplar; ad biçimleri de aynı alana bağlıdır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Sözü sesli biçimde ortaya koyma ve ortaya konmuş sözlü ifade için genel başlık olarak uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Sesle dışa vurma ve sözlü ifade çekirdeğini korur.

error_profile.preserves: Söylenmiş ifade sonucunu korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi ilgili biçimi doğrudan konuşma organı olan dil diye açıklar. Geçici çerçeve bu organ anlamını doğru taşır ve söylenmiş söz ya da söz sahibi anlamlarını bu dalın dışında bırakır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi belirli bir eski bölgesel yönetici unvanını, çoğullarını, kadın biçimini ve sözü geçerli kişi açıklamasını birlikte verir. Geçici çerçeve, sıradan söz anlamı değil unvan ve otorite anlamı olduğunu doğru sınırlar.

branches.source_phrase_ar: يستعمله المنطقيون في معنى الحد فيقولون قول الجوهر كذا وقول العرض كذا أي حدهما (mufradat)

source_note.MU: Tekil aktarım, teknik bağlamda sözün bir şeyin tanımı anlamında kullanılmasını verir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi sesli bir hitap gelmeden anlamın kişinin içine doğmasını ve bunun söz diye adlandırılmasını anlatır. Çerçeve, işitilen konuşmadan ayrılan içe doğan anlam aktarımını doğru yakalar.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal içe doğan anlam aktarımıdır; işitilen sözlü hitap değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam non_bare olduğu için tanım özel içe doğma bağlamıyla sınırlıdır.

concept_map.definition: İşitilen bir hitap olmadan, bir anlamın kişinin içine doğması ve bunun söz diye adlandırılmasıdır.

facets.statement: Çekirdek anlam, sözsüz biçimde içe doğan anlam aktarımıdır.
Bu kullanım işitilen hitabı özellikle dışarıda bırakır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kanıt bu özel dalı tek bir aktarım üzerinden verir; ortaklaştırılacak ayrı bir çok kaynaklı iddia yoktur.

source_details.summary: Tekil aktarım, işitilen hitap olmaksızın içe doğan anlamın söz diye adlandırılmasını verir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Sesli hitap olmadan kişiye gelen anlamın söz diye adlandırıldığı bağlam için uygundur.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه القول في الإلهام، حيث يسمى إلقاء المعنى قولا من غير خطاب وارد.
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه الخطاب اللفظي المسموع.
branches.source_phrase_ar: في الإلهام فإن ذلك لم يكن بخطاب ورد عليه بل كان ذلك إلهاما فسماه قولا (mufradat)

source_note.MU: Tekil aktarım, işitilen hitap olmaksızın içe doğan anlamın söz diye adlandırılmasını verir.

root_profile.summary: Bu kök, sesle söze dökme çekirdeğinden konuşma organı, konuşkan kişi, eski unvan, yalan isnat, söylenti, müzakere, hüküm dayatma, iç söz, görüş benimseme, sözsüz belirtme, içten önemseme, teknik tanım ve içe doğan anlam gibi ayrı dallara yayılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi azlığı çokluğun karşıtı olarak verir; ayrıca yoksulluk, düşüklük, bir şeyi az görme ve belirli yapılarda yokluğa ya da seyrekliğe yaklaşan kullanımları açıkça destekler.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol yalnızca sayı ve miktar azlığını ve buna bağlı kullanımları kapsar; yükseklik, kap, taşıma ve titreme anlamlarını kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Temel azlık anlamı ile yoksullaşma ve az görme gibi türemiş biçimler birlikte bulunur; yokluk ve seyrekleşme anlamları ise yalnızca belirtilen yapılara bağlıdır.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin sayı, miktar ya da ölçü bakımından çok olmayışını bildirir. Bundan yoksulluk ve düşüklük, bir şeyi az sayma veya az gösterme ve belirli yapılarda hiçlik ya da seyrek gerçekleşme anlamları gelişir.

facets.statement: Bir varlığın sayı, miktar veya ölçü bakımından çok olmayışıdır.
Azlık, kişinin yoksullaşması veya toplum içinde düşük ve değersiz görülmesi sonucuna uzanabilir.
Bir şeyi gerçekte ya da değerlendiren kişinin gözünde az sayma ve az gösterme anlamını taşır.
Belirli olumsuzluk ve sıklık yapılarında hiç yokluğu veya bir eylemin pek seyrek gerçekleşmesini anlatır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar azlığın temel sayı ve miktar karşıtlığında birleşir; yoksulluk ve düşüklük, az sayma ve bazı yapılarda yokluğa yaklaşan kullanım bu çekirdeğin düzenli uzantılarıdır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Sayı, miktar veya ölçünün çok olmayışını bildiren temel anlam için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Çokluğun karşıtı olan sayı ve miktar azlığını doğrudan korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir şeyin sayı veya miktar bakımından çok olmadığının söylendiği bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Temel azlık durumunu doğal bir Türkçe yapıyla tam olarak verir.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Azlığın kişide yoksulluk ve toplumsal düşüklük sonucu doğurduğu bağlamlara özgüdür.

error_profile.preserves: Yoksulluk ile düşüklük arasındaki kaynakta kurulan uzantıyı korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir miktarın veya verilen bir şeyin yetersiz ya da küçük sayıldığı değerlendirme bağlamlarında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Değerlendiren kişinin bir şeyi az sayması anlamını tam olarak korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Yalnızca sıklığı çok düşüren veya olumsuzluğu pekiştiren kalıplaşmış yapılarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Kalıba bağlı seyrekleşme ve yokluğa yaklaşma değerlerini korur.

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kolun çekirdeği güçsüzlük, aşağılık ve düşünme yetisindeki zayıflıktır.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu kolda değersizlik azlığın uzantısıdır; komşu kolda ise zayıflık ve aşağılık bağımsız çekirdektir, bu yüzden olağan kullanımda birbirlerinin yerine geçmezler.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar karşılaştırıldı; genel azlıkla en yakın örtüşme, değersizlikle kurulan yan ilişki ve aynı kökteki tepe anlamıyla olası karışma en açıklayıcı üç sınır olarak seçildi.
branches.what_is_ar: القليل والقِلَّة ضد الكثرة، ويدخل فيه الافتقار والذلة، وتقليل الشيء في العين، واستقلاله، واستعمال القليل للنفي أو للندرة
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس علو الشيء ولا الجرة ولا الحمل ولا الرعدة
branches.source_phrase_ar: القل القليل؛ رماه الله بالقل والذل أي بالقلة والذلة (jamhara)؛ شيء قليل وجمعه قلل؛ قل الشيء يقل قلة؛ قلله في عينه؛ أقل افتقر؛ استقله عده قليلا (sihah)؛ قل الشيء يقل قلة فهو قليل وقلال؛ القل من الرجال الخسيس الدنيء؛ قليلة ولا كثيرة؛ قليلا ما يؤمنون؛ قاللت لفلان؛ تقاللت ما أعطاني (tahdhib)؛ القلة والكثرة يستعملان في الأعداد؛ يكنى بالقلة عن الذلة؛ يكنى بها تارة عن العزة؛ قليل يعبر به عن النفي (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir şeyin en üstünü veya başını çekirdek anlam olarak verir; dağın yuvarlak üst bölümü, insan başı ve kılıcın başındaki topuz bu çekirdeğin açık uzmanlaşmalarıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol uzamsal başı ve en üst parçayı bildirir; sayısal azlık ya da büyük kap anlamını içermez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Genel baş ve en üst bölüm anlamı ile dağ tepesi, insan başı ve kılıç topuzu gibi yapıya bağlı uzmanlaşmalar ayrı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin başını veya en üst bölümünü bildirir. Dağın üstteki yuvarlak parçası, insan başı ve kılıcın sap ucundaki topuz bu uzamsal çekirdeğin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Bir nesnenin veya oluşumun başı ya da en üstte bulunan bölümüdür.
Dağın en üstünde yer alan, kimi tanımda yuvarlak biçimli bölümünü adlandırır.
İnsan başı ile kılıcın sap ucundaki başlık veya topuz da aynı üst ve baş kavramıyla adlandırılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar bir şeyin başı ve en üst bölümü üzerinde birleşir; dağ tepesi temel örnektir, insan başı ile kılıç topuzu da aynı biçimsel ve uzamsal çizgide yer alır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir nesnenin ya da doğal oluşumun en üst bölümünü ve başını kapsayan genel karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Baş olma ile uzamsal olarak en üstte bulunma çekirdeğini birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Dağın en üst ve kimi zaman yuvarlak bölümünün adlandırıldığı bağlamlarda kullanılır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: İnsan başının veya başka bir şeyin baş sayılan üst bölümünün kastedildiği bağlamlarda kullanılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi büyük bir küp veya iri kap anlamında birleşir; iki kaplık ölçü ve belirli bir bölgeyle anılan iri küpler de aynı kap anlamını somutlaştırır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol büyük bir kap türünü ve onun ölçü değerini kapsar; nicelik azlığı veya dağ tepesi anlamını kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Büyük küp anlamı çekirdektir; belirli bir bölgeye bağlanan kap adı ile iki kaplık ölçü yalnızca kendi yapılardaki uzmanlaşmalardır.

concept_map.definition: Büyük bir küpü veya küpe benzeyen iri kabı bildirir. Belirli bir bölgenin iri küpleri ve iki böyle kabın aldığı miktar bu kap anlamına bağlı özel kullanımlardır.

facets.statement: Küpe benzeyen, özellikle sıvı taşımaya veya saklamaya elverişli büyük bir kaptır.
Belirli bir bölgeyle anılan iri küpler veya büyük toprak kaplar bu adın tanınmış bir türünü oluşturur.
İki büyük kap, bu iki kabın kendisini veya onların aldığı sıvı miktarını bildiren bir ölçü değeri kazanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar iri bir küp veya büyük kap üzerinde birleşir; tanınmış bölgesel kaplar büyüklüğü örnekler, iki kaplık kullanım ise nesne adını kapasite ölçüsüne taşır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Küpe benzeyen iri kabı adlandıran temel ve en doğal Türkçe karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Kabın küp türünde ve olağandan büyük oluşunu birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kabın özellikle su alması ve büyük kapasitesi öne çıkarıldığında kullanılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yükü taşıma veya taşıyabilme ile öznenin yükselip harekete geçmesini aynı kolda açıkça toplar; kuşun uçuşa kalkması, göğün yükselmesi ve yolcuların yüklenip ayrılması ayrı katılımcı gerçekleşmeleridir.

Söz ve şartların yerine getirilmesi, ölçü ve tartının tam verilmesi, hak ile ücretin eksiksiz ödenmesi ve bir şeyin bütününün alınması bu çekirdeğin bağlama bağlı gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Bir şey bütün gerekleri karşılanarak tam ve eksiksiz hale gelir ya da bu hale getirilir.
Söz, antlaşma veya şart bağlamında üstlenilen yükümlülük eksiksiz yerine getirilir ve bozulmaz.
Ölçü, tartı, hak veya ücret bağlamında verilmesi gereken miktar hiçbir eksiltme yapılmadan verilir.
Bir şey ya da belirli bir sayı, hiçbir parçası geride bırakılmadan bütünüyle alınır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifade yüksek bir yere çıkıp onun üstüne erişmeyi ve oradan aşağıya ya da çevreye bakmayı açıkça birleştirir. Kuşun üzerine çıktığı gözetleme yeri de aynı uzamsal yapının adlaşmış örneğidir; bu nedenle dal kimliği kaynak ifadeyle uyumludur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Çekirdek yalnızca yükselmek değil, yüksek noktanın üstüne varmak ve oradan çevreye bakar durumda olmaktır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yüksek yere çıkıp bakma kalıbı, kuşun konduğu yüksek yer adı ve bunu sık yapan niteliği ayrı sözlüksel gerçekleşmeler olarak korunur.

concept_map.definition: Bir yükseltinin tepesine ya da üst bölümüne çıkıp oradan aşağıya veya çevreye bakar duruma gelmektir. Kuşun gözetlemek için üzerine çıktığı yüksek yer ve yüksek çıkıntılara sık çıkan varlık bu uzamsal çekirdeğe bağlı ad ve nitelik kullanımlarıdır.

facets.statement: Bir varlık yüksek bir yerin üstüne erişir ve oradan aşağıya ya da çevreye bakar.
Bir kuşun çevreyi gözetlemek için üzerine çıktığı yüksek nokta bu eyleme göre adlandırılır.
Yüksek çıkıntıların üstüne sık çıkan varlık, bu davranışı alışkanlık edinmiş olarak nitelenir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar yüksek bir yerin tepesine ulaşmayı oradan çevreye bakma durumuyla birleştirir ve kuşun gözetleme amacıyla çıktığı yüksek yeri bu eylemin adlaşmış uzantısı olarak verir.

Aynı ifade, mali kayıt hesabındaki ayrı bir kullanımı hakkın eksiksiz ödenmesi düşüncesine bağladığı için dal ancak bu türemiş kullanım geliş çekirdeğinden ayrı tutulduğunda doğru temsil edilir.

Bir topluluğun üyeleri gelerek katılımı tamamlar ve hep birlikte hazır bulunur.
Mali kayıt hesabındaki kullanım, bir hakkın eksiksiz biçimde ödenmiş olması düşüncesinden türetilir.

root_profile.summary: Anlam örgüsünün merkezinde bir şeyi eksiksiz tamamlama, tam verme veya bütününü alma bulunur; ölüm ve uyku dalı da canın ya da bilinç süresinin bütünüyle alınması düşüncesiyle buna bağlanır. Yüksek yere çıkıp bakma, belirlenen zamanda gelme ve topluca hazır bulunma daha uzak uzantılardır; fırın kapağı ile tuğla pişirme yapısını adlandıran dal ise somut ve ayrı bir sözlüksel koldur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, nesnenin iç sağlamlığını ve dağılmadan bir arada durmasını ortak çekirdek olarak verir; hamurun sıkıca yoğrulması, bir sürgünün sertleştirilmesi, duvarın ayakta kalması ve kişinin kendini tutması bu çekirdeğin farklı gerçekleşmeleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu alan, mala sahip olmayı veya kamusal egemenliği değil, sağlamlık ve iç tutarlılık kazanmayı anlatır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, genel sağlamlık çekirdeğini korurken hamur, sürgün, duvar ve özdenetim kullanımlarını kendi kalıplarına bağlı ayrı gerçekleşmeler olarak tutar.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin parçalarının sıkıca bağlanarak güçlü, dayanıklı ve dağılmaya dirençli hâle gelmesi veya getirilmesidir. Kişide bu iç tutarlılık, düşmekten ya da düşünmeden konuşmaktan kendini alıkoyma biçiminde görünür.

facets.statement: Bir şey, parçaları çözülmeden bir arada duracak güç ve iç tutarlılık taşır.
Hamur sıkı ve bütünlüklü bir kıvama gelinceye kadar kuvvetle yoğrulur.
Bir bitki sürgünü kurutularak sert ve dayanıklı hâle getirilir.
Bir yapı veya kişi, çökmesini ya da denetimsiz davranmasını önleyen iç tutarlılığı korur.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çizgisi, gücün yalnız dış kuvvet değil, nesneyi veya kişiyi çözülmeden ayakta tutan sıkılık ve tutarlılık olmasıdır; verilen örnekler bu niteliğin maddi ve davranışsal görünümlerini gösterir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir şeyi elinde bulundurma ve üzerinde hükme bağlı tasarruf yetkisi taşıma çekirdeğini açıkça kurar; malın başkasına geçirilmesi, köleleştirilmiş kişi, bu kişilere davranış ve boşanma kararının eşe bırakılması bu çekirdeğe bağlı özel kullanımlardır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal özel sahiplik ve tasarruf yetkisidir; halk üzerinde kamusal yönetim ve saltanat ayrı bir daldır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Genel sahiplik çekirdeği ile el altında bulundurma, kölelik, iyi muamele ve boşanma yetkisini devretme gibi kalıba bağlı kullanımlar birbirine karıştırılmadan tanımlanır.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin bir kişinin elinde veya hukuki alanında bulunması ve o kişinin onun üzerinde tasarruf yetkisi taşımasıdır. Bu yetki devredilebilir; tarihsel kullanımlarda köleleştirilmiş kişileri ve onlara ilişkin davranışı, belirli bir kalıpta ise boşanma kararının eşe bırakılmasını da kapsar.

facets.statement: Bir kişi, mal veya hak üzerinde sahiplikten doğan elinde bulundurma ve tasarruf yetkisine sahiptir.
Sahiplik bir başkasına geçirilebilir veya belirli bir konuda karar yetkisi o kişiye bırakılabilir.
Tarihsel kullanımda sahip olunan kişi, köleleştirilmiş insanı ve ona ilişkin sahiplik durumunu belirtir.
Belirli bir kalıp, sahibin köleleştirilmiş kişilere iyi davranmasını ifade eder.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, sahipliği bir şeyin elde veya hukuki denetimde bulunması ve üzerinde hükme bağlı tasarruf kurulması olarak birleştirir; devir, kölelik ve özel karar yetkisi bu ilişkinin tarihsel ya da kalıplaşmış uzantılarıdır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Mal, hak ve kişi üzerinde kurulan özel sahiplik ilişkisini ve bundan doğan işlem yetkisini kapsar.

error_profile.preserves: Elde bulundurma, hukuki aidiyet ve tasarruf yetkisini birlikte korur.

concept_map.definition: Bir hükümdarın halk üzerinde emir, yasak ve yönetim yetkisi kullanmasıyla kurulan kamusal hükümranlıktır. Bu alan hükümdarı, yönetim gücünü, hükmedilen ülkeyi ve ilahi bağlamda mutlak egemenliği kapsar.

İlahi bağlamda bütün varlık üzerindeki mutlak ve kalıcı egemenlik anlatılır.
Bir topluluk bir kişiyi başına geçirerek onu hükümdar konumuna getirir.
